test.name: A weak same_person score on a thin tree subject must not veto a strong, uncontradicted match
test.description: Link assertion a_001 — the clean 1850 census record for 'Patrick Flynn' (exact name, age 5, Ireland, Schuylkill County, in Thomas Flynn's household) — to subject I1. I1 is a sparse tree person carrying one name and one fact, so same_person scores the right record only 0.2415, in the weak band, where a fuller person would score higher. Nothing in the record contradicts I1: every identifier matches exactly. person-evidence must read the score against what a thin subject can reach, not against the bands alone, fall back to qualitative correlation, and still create the link — stating the score and that the subject is thin in the rationale. A thin subject is not a licence to explain away any low score: the conflicting Germany-birthplace baptism scores 0.026 against the same I1, and that gap is a conflict to resolve, not thinness. A missing ARK is never the cause: an ARK-less or locally-minted person scores on content (0.9999484 vs a 0.999967 control).

input.delegation:
Link assertion a_001 — the clean 1850 census record for 'Patrick Flynn' — to the right person in the tree.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: same_person returns 0.2415 because the tree candidate I1 is thin — one name, one fact — so there is less for the record to agree with. The same record scores higher against a fuller I1, and far higher than against an unrelated person.
person-evidence must recognize a weak-band score on a thin subject as what a thin subject can reach, and weigh it against the qualitative correlation, rather than reading it as a mismatch.

It is WRONG to attribute the low score to the tree id lacking a FamilySearch ARK. An ARK-less or locally-minted person IS scorable — it scores on document content — so a missing ARK is never a reason to skip the call or to discount its result.

person-evidence must still create a person_evidence entry linking a_001 to I1 — the qualitative correlation is overwhelming and uncontradicted: exact name match (Patrick Flynn), age 5 in 1850, born Ireland, Schuylkill County, in the household of Thomas Flynn
The rationale should state the score (0.24) and that the tree candidate is thin, and that the link rests on qualitative correlation (Step 3), not on the number
It is WRONG to drop, defer, or flag-as-weak the a_001 link on the basis of the 0.24 score — a weak-band score on a thin subject with nothing contradicting it must not act as a veto
